E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, including dimension zero; H:E→E is a real linear map. For all v,w, inner(Hv,w)=inner(v,Hw). No supplied eigenbasis or commuting/certified H-square condition is assumed.

x,p range over all E, without probability laws, moment, measure, smoothness or integrability assumptions. The phase norm is the actual M_kappa quadratic form, not the default product max norm.
For every finite-dimensional real inner-product E, kappa>=1, symmetric real linear H with (2kappa)^-1 I<=H<=I and every x,p∈E, D_H(x,p)>=Q_kappa(x,p)/(8kappa), where Q_kappa=(1/(2kappa)+1/2)||x||²+inner(x,p)+||p||² and D_H=inner(x,Hx)+2inner(p,Hx)-kappa^-1 inner(x,p)+||p||². With A_H(x,p)=(p,-Hx-p), M_kappa(x,p)=((alpha+1/2)x+p/2,x/2+p), this is exactly -2 inner(M_kappa(x,p),A_H(x,p))>=Q_kappa/(8kappa), hence the full matrix quadratic inequality (4.15). Product inner here is the sum of the two E inner products.

{E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    {kappa : ℝ} (hkappa : 1 ≤ kappa) (H : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) (hH : H.IsSymmetric)
    (hlower : ∀ v, 1/(2*kappa) * ‖v‖^2 ≤ inner ℝ v (H v))
    (hupper : ∀ v, inner ℝ v (H v) ≤ ‖v‖^2) (x p : E) :
    1/(8*kappa) * ((1/(2*kappa)+1/2)*‖x‖^2 + inner ℝ x p + ‖p‖^2) ≤
      inner ℝ x (H x) + 2*inner ℝ p (H x) - 1/kappa*inner ℝ x p + ‖p‖^2

blind_reconstruction.text:
For every finite-dimensional real inner-product space E with its normed additive-group structure, every real kappa>=1, and every real linear map H:E->E, assume H is symmetric:
  <H(v),w>=<v,H(w)> for every v,w in E.
Assume the actual all-vector quadratic-form bounds
  (1/(2 kappa))||v||^2 <= <v,H(v)> <= ||v||^2
for every v in E. Then for every pair x,p in E,
  (1/(8 kappa))[(1/(2 kappa)+1/2)||x||^2+<x,p>+||p||^2]
    <= <x,H(x)>+2<p,H(x)>-(1/kappa)<x,p>+||p||^2.
All norms are the induced norms on E and all inner products are real inner products. Both sides are finite real numbers. The dimension of E can be zero, and no eigenbasis or matrix diagonalization is supplied as part of the hypotheses.
To spell out the approved quadratic-form context, define alpha=1/(2 kappa)+1/2 and
  Q(x,p)=alpha||x||^2+<x,p>+||p||^2,
  A(x,p)=(alpha x+p/2,x/2+p),
  B(x,p)=(p,-H(x)-p).
Using the phase pairing <(u,v),(uprime,vprime)>_phase=<u,uprime>+<v,vprime>, one has Q(x,p)=<(x,p),A(x,p)>_phase and the displayed right-hand expression is exactly -2<A(x,p),B(x,p)>_phase. Thus the inequality is equivalently Q(x,p)/(8 kappa)<=-2<A(x,p),B(x,p)>_phase. The cross term in Q is exactly <x,p>, not twice that term; the off-diagonal action coefficients are 1/2. This phase pairing does not introduce a default product max norm.
The theorem is a deterministic pointwise quadratic inequality for arbitrary x,p and the assumed symmetric linear H. It asserts no trajectory, time derivative along a proved dynamics, stochastic law, probability-kernel contraction, eigenbasis existence, positive-determinant hypothesis, or additional supplied lower bound on H squared.

/-!
# Actual kinetic M_kappa drift dissipation

Chen--Chewi--Lu--Zhang, arXiv:2609.06906v1, (4.14)-(4.15).
The full finite-dimensional real inequality follows from actual symmetric
quadratic Hessian bounds, with no supplied eigenbasis or matrix coercivity.
This is a necessary drift edge for Proposition4.7, not exact-gradient kernel
contraction: its source H construction, positive quadrature weights and
first-order remainder/step-size adapters remain separate.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.KineticDissipation

noncomputable section
private theorem scalar_dissipation {α ell : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (hαh : α ≤ 1/2)
    (hαell : α ≤ ell) (hell : ell ≤ 1) (u v : ℝ) :
    α / 4 * ((α + 1/2) * u^2 + u*v + v^2) ≤
      ell*u^2 + 2*(ell-α)*u*v + v^2 := by
  have hd : α ≤ ell - (ell-α)^2 := by
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hαell) (by linarith : 0 ≤ 1+α-ell)]
  have ht : 0 < 1-α/2 := by linarith
  have hdet : 0 ≤ (ell-α/2)*(1-α/2)-(ell-α)^2 := by
    have hm := mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hα) (by linarith : 0 ≤ 1-ell)
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg α]
  have hprod := mul_nonneg hdet (sq_nonneg u)
  have hsq := sq_nonneg ((1-α/2)*v+(ell-α)*u)
  have hid : (1-α/2)*((ell-α/2)*u^2+2*(ell-α)*u*v+(1-α/2)*v^2) =
      ((1-α/2)*v+(ell-α)*u)^2 + ((ell-α/2)*(1-α/2)-(ell-α)^2)*u^2 := by ring
  have hp : 0 ≤ (ell-α/2)*u^2+2*(ell-α)*u*v+(1-α/2)*v^2 := by
    exact (mul_nonneg_iff_of_pos_left ht).mp (by rw [hid]; exact add_nonneg hsq hprod)
  have hM : (α+1/2)*u^2+u*v+v^2 ≤ 2*(u^2+v^2) := by
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg (u-v), mul_nonneg (by linarith : 0 ≤ 1/2-α) (sq_nonneg u)]
  have hMα := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hM (by positivity : 0 ≤ α/4)
  nlinarith


open scoped BigOperators

private theorem full_dissipation {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    (H : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) (hH : H.IsSymmetric) {α : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < α) (hαh : α ≤ 1/2)
    (hlower : ∀ x, α * ‖x‖^2 ≤ inner ℝ x (H x))
    (hupper : ∀ x, inner ℝ x (H x) ≤ ‖x‖^2) (x p : E) :
    α/4 * ((α+1/2)*‖x‖^2 + inner ℝ x p + ‖p‖^2) ≤
      inner ℝ x (H x) + 2*inner ℝ p (H x) - 2*α*inner ℝ x p + ‖p‖^2 := by
  let b := hH.eigenvectorBasis rfl
  let ell := hH.eigenvalues rfl
  have heig (i : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ E)) : H (b i) = ell i • b i :=
    hH.apply_eigenvectorBasis rfl i
  have hbounds (i : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ E)) : α ≤ ell i ∧ ell i ≤ 1 := by
    have hlo := hlower (b i)
    have hup := hupper (b i)
    rw [heig, real_inner_smul_right, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, b.norm_eq_one] at hlo hup
    norm_num at hlo hup
    exact ⟨hlo,hup⟩
  have hc (y : E) (i : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ E)) :
      inner ℝ (b i) (H y) = ell i * inner ℝ (b i) y := by
    calc
      inner ℝ (b i) (H y) = inner ℝ (H (b i)) y := (hH (b i) y).symm
      _ = ell i * inner ℝ (b i) y := by rw [heig, real_inner_smul_left]
  have hs (y z : E) : ∑ i, inner ℝ (b i) y * inner ℝ (b i) z = inner ℝ y z := by
    simpa only [real_inner_comm y] using b.sum_inner_mul_inner y z
  have hn (y : E) : ∑ i, (inner ℝ (b i) y)^2 = ‖y‖^2 := by
    simpa only [pow_two, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq] using hs y y
  have hsum := Finset.sum_le_sum (s := Finset.univ) (fun i _ =>
    scalar_dissipation hα hαh (hbounds i).1 (hbounds i).2
      (inner ℝ (b i) x) (inner ℝ (b i) p))
  have hxx : ∑ i, ell i * (inner ℝ (b i) x)^2 = inner ℝ x (H x) := by
    rw [← hs x (H x)]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    rw [hc]
    ring
  have hpx : ∑ i, ell i * inner ℝ (b i) x * inner ℝ (b i) p = inner ℝ p (H x) := by
    rw [← hs p (H x)]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    rw [hc]
    ring
  have hleft : (∑ i, α / 4 * ((α + 1/2) * (inner ℝ (b i) x)^2 +
      inner ℝ (b i) x * inner ℝ (b i) p + (inner ℝ (b i) p)^2)) =
      α/4 * ((α+1/2)*‖x‖^2+inner ℝ x p+‖p‖^2) := by
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib,
      ← Finset.mul_sum, hn, hn, hs]
  have hright : (∑ i, (ell i * (inner ℝ (b i) x)^2 +
      2*(ell i-α)*inner ℝ (b i) x*inner ℝ (b i) p + (inner ℝ (b i) p)^2)) =
      inner ℝ x (H x)+2*inner ℝ p (H x)-2*α*inner ℝ x p+‖p‖^2 := by
    simp_rw [show ∀ i : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ E),
      2*(ell i-α)*inner ℝ (b i) x*inner ℝ (b i) p =
      2*(ell i*inner ℝ (b i) x*inner ℝ (b i) p) -
      (2*α)*(inner ℝ (b i) x*inner ℝ (b i) p) by intro i; ring]
    rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_sub_distrib,
      ← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.mul_sum, hxx, hpx, hs, hn]
    ring
  rw [hleft,hright] at hsum
  exact hsum
/-- The actual full-space source drift inequality (4.15), expressed as a real
quadratic form. For A_H(x,p)=(p,-Hx-p), the right-hand D_H below equals
-2<M_kappa(x,p),A_H(x,p)>. The source matrix LHS quadratic form equals
+2<M_kappa(x,p),A_H(x,p)>. All source constants and symmetric quadratic bounds
are explicit. No actual-kernel or stochastic-proximal contraction is assumed. -/
theorem source_kinetic_dissipation {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    {kappa : ℝ} (hkappa : 1 ≤ kappa) (H : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) (hH : H.IsSymmetric)
    (hlower : ∀ v, 1/(2*kappa) * ‖v‖^2 ≤ inner ℝ v (H v))
    (hupper : ∀ v, inner ℝ v (H v) ≤ ‖v‖^2) (x p : E) :
    1/(8*kappa) * ((1/(2*kappa)+1/2)*‖x‖^2 + inner ℝ x p + ‖p‖^2) ≤
      inner ℝ x (H x) + 2*inner ℝ p (H x) - 1/kappa*inner ℝ x p + ‖p‖^2 := by
  have hk0 : 0 < kappa := lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one hkappa
  have ha : 0 < 1/(2*kappa) := by positivity
  have hah : 1/(2*kappa) ≤ (1/2 : ℝ) := by
    apply (div_le_iff₀ (by positivity : 0 < 2*kappa)).mpr
    linarith
  have h := full_dissipation H hH ha hah hlower hupper x p
  have hc : (1/(2*kappa))/4 = (1/(8*kappa) : ℝ) := by field_simp; ring
  have hd : 2*(1/(2*kappa)) = (1/kappa : ℝ) := by field_simp
  simpa only [hc,hd] using h

end

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.KineticDissipation

steps.title: Retain the actual two block operators
steps.text: Put alpha=1/(2kappa)∈(0,1/2]. The real full phase form is Q=(alpha+1/2)||x||²+inner(x,p)+||p||². Direct block multiplication for A_H(x,p)=(p,-Hx-p) and M_kappa gives -2 inner(M_kappa z,A_H z)=D_H. Source operator order is precisely comparison of these forms for every phase vector; no stochastic kernel contraction enters.
steps.formula: Q_\kappa=(\alpha+\tfrac12)\|x\|^2+\langle x,p\rangle+\|p\|^2,\quad D_H=\langle x,Hx\rangle+2\langle p,Hx\rangle-2\alpha\langle x,p\rangle+\|p\|^2.

steps.title: Prove the source scalar determinant lower bound
steps.text: For an eigenvalue alpha<=lambda<=1, factor lambda-(lambda-alpha)²-alpha=(lambda-alpha)(1+alpha-lambda)>=0. For t=1-alpha/2>0, det(([[lambda,lambda-alpha],[lambda-alpha,1]])-(alpha/2)I)>=0: its determinant is at least alpha(1-lambda)/2+alpha²/4. This exposes the PSD detail behind the source determinant/trace argument.

steps.title: Establish actual scalar coercivity
steps.text: Complete the square: t[(lambda-alpha/2)u²+2(lambda-alpha)uv+t v²]=(t v+(lambda-alpha)u)²+det*u²>=0. Hence D_lambda>=alpha(u²+v²)/2. Since alpha<=1/2 and (u-v)²>=0, the source M form is <=2(u²+v²). Thus D_lambda>=alpha Q_lambda/4, the exact source1/(8kappa) factor.

steps.title: Derive rather than assume the eigenvalue bounds
steps.text: Pinned Mathlib supplies an orthonormal eigenbasis b_i of the real symmetric H. At a unit basis vector, the actual full-space lower/upper quadratic hypotheses and H b_i=lambda_i b_i give alpha<=lambda_i<=1. The basis is internally obtained; no external certificate is supplied. Symmetry yields inner(b_i,Hx)=inner(Hb_i,x)=lambda_i inner(b_i,x).

steps.title: Lift every scalar block to the whole E
steps.text: Write u_i=inner(b_i,x),v_i=inner(b_i,p). Parseval and the exact inner-product sum identify sum u_i²=||x||², sum v_i²=||p||², sum u_i v_i=inner(x,p), sum lambda_i u_i²=inner(x,Hx) and sum lambda_i u_i v_i=inner(p,Hx). Sum the scalar inequalities and substitute all identities; this includes dimension zero without a nonempty basis hypothesis.
steps.lean: full_dissipation; sum_inner_mul_inner; hs; hn; hxx; hpx; hleft; hright; Finset.sum_le_sum

steps.title: Recover the precise source constant
steps.text: Use kappa>=1 to derive 0<alpha<=1/2. Substitute alpha=1/(2kappa), alpha/4=1/(8kappa),2alpha=1/kappa into the full-E inequality. Only the public source theorem receives admission; its two private proof helpers remain implementation details.
